Welcome to Rushey Green Primary School
We are proud to be a Rights Respecting Gold Award School, serving our children and the local community.
I would like to take the opportunity to extend a warm welcome to you and your children as Interim Headteacher of Rushey Green Primary School - a place where staff and children feel safe, happy, challenged and supported to achieve their full potential.
Rushey Green is a three-form entry primary school located in the heart of Catford. We are committed to providing a friendly, caring, supportive environment where children are valued and given the self belief to be their very best. I am proud to lead a team who are fully committed to children’s physical and emotional wellbeing whilst aspiring for all to do their best.
We believe in building strong partnerships - the school is well supported by our governors and parents. We have an active RGSA and have strong links with other local primary schools in the area.
Our Curriculum
Safeguarding
Calendar
Admissions
Primary schools in Lewisham are among the top-performing schools in the country. Last year, children leaving primary schools in Lewisham achieved the fourth-best results in the country.
We are more than happy to offer tours of the school for in-year admissions and welcome any questions or queries; admin@rusheygreen.lewisham.sch.uk.
If you are offered a place at Rushey Green, you will be invited in to have an admissions interview where you can look round the school and meet with the Interim Headteacher before you start.

pageCache.pageTitle: Vision and Values | Rushey Green Primary School
pageCache.text:
Vision and Values
Our Vision
Growing Future Leaders
Rushey Green is a place where staff and pupils feel safe, happy, challenged and supported to achieve their full potential. Our vision is to create a school community where pupils grow into caring, responsible and proud individuals who are united. By championing equity and promoting physical and emotional well-being, we equip our pupils with knowledge, skills, self-belief and resilience (thriving) to be critical thinkers, prepared for tomorrow’s world.
We strive to create a safe, inclusive and supportive learning environment where every pupil feels valued, represented and empowered.
We foster a love of learning through our knowledge rich curriculum, experiences and enrichment - we believe in nurturing the unique talents and abilities of each pupil. At Rushey Green, we are committed to building strong partnerships with families and the wider community.
Our School Values
At Rushey Green our school values are the guiding principles that shape how our children learn, behave, and grow together. We believe they help everyone understand what the school stands for and create a positive, consistent culture.
Resilience
Unity
Self-belief
Honesty
Empathy
Yearning to Learn
Together, we believe these values help children become kind, confident, and motivated learners who contribute positively to our school community.

Welcome to Rushey Green
Welcome to Rushey Green Primary School
We are proud to be a Rights Respecting Gold Award School, serving our children and the local community.
I would like to take the opportunity to extend a warm welcome to you and your children as Interim Headteacher of Rushey Green Primary School - a place where staff and children feel safe, happy, challenged and supported to achieve their full potential.
Rushey Green is a three-form entry primary school located in the heart of Catford. We are committed to providing a friendly, caring, supportive environment where children are valued and given the self belief to be their very best. I am proud to lead a team who are fully committed to children’s physical and emotional wellbeing whilst aspiring for all to do their best.
We believe in building strong partnerships - the school is well supported by our governors and parents. We have an active RGSA and have strong links with other local primary schools in the area.
Rushey Green is committed to safeguarding. We have high expectations and it is important to us that the children at Rushey Green are happy, confident, resilient (thriving) and enjoy learning. We ensure that all learning is purposeful, engaging and challenging. Our curriculum is inclusive and exciting, providing children with a range of experiences which seek to spark curiosity and nurture talents.
Our aim is for children to have a deeper understanding of the world around them and to become responsible and caring citizens of the future.
We hope that during your child’s time at Rushey Green they will become confident, inquisitive, proud individuals. We endeavour to work closely with parents and families to achieve the best provision for every individual.
Our website is your first opportunity to find out lots of information about our school, however, we would love you to visit the school if you are thinking of choosing Rushey Green for your child’s setting - to experience the school environment and ethos for yourselves.
Please contact our school office to make an appointment.
Mrs Rachel Waite

Music
Subjects
Music at Rushey Green
The children at Rushey Green have one lesson of class music a week. In their lessons pupils learn recorder, drumming and chime bars/glockenspiel/ xylophone for the purpose of leading them on to learn piano or a wind instrument. Our children benefit from music as a whole in supporting their mental and emotional development. Music lessons include reading and writing music using standard notation as well as exploring graphic scores. In year 6 the children compose and produce music using music technology. The Year 4’s receive 1 year of Violin tuition. The children are able to learn individual instruments with teachers from the Lewisham music service. The instruments learned are flute,clarinet, saxophone, trumpet, guitar, drum kit, violin and piano. The children have singing assemblies where year groups sing a variety of songs covering the seasons, celebrations and a wide variety of genres.
Rushey green has school choirs for KS1 and KS2 that perform extensively in the community and at interschool festivals and concerts. Our choirs have performed in local churches, Gospel concerts, Opera concerts, at the Blackheath Halls and at the O2. Rushey Green has a school band where musicians learning instruments can rehearse and learn band skills. The band performs in concerts and school events.

Computing
Subjects
Computing at Rushey Green
Purple Mash is a child‑friendly online space where children can learn important computer skills in a safe and fun way. It’s designed especially for primary schools, so everything is age‑appropriate and easy for young learners to use.
Purple Mash introduces children to the three key strands of the primary computing curriculum in a way that feels simple, engaging and accessible for families. Each strand supports a different part of children’s digital learning, and together they help build confidence, creativity and safe online habits.
Throughout their time at Rushey Green, pupils will experience a wide range of computing units, including the following:
Coding: Making a simple program
Word processing
Touch typing
Spreadsheets
Simulations
Presentations
Blogging
Digital Art and Design

Online Safety

Maths
Subjects
Maths at Rushey Green
At Rushey Green, the maths curriculum is designed to be ambitious, inclusive and rooted in the belief that every child can achieve highly in mathematics. Lessons are practical, engaging and built around exploration, giving children the chance to investigate ideas, talk about their thinking and make meaningful connections between concepts. This approach helps pupils see the bigger picture, deepen their understanding and develop confidence as mathematical thinkers.
The curriculum is shaped and strengthened by guidance from the National Centre for Excellence in the Teaching of Mathematics (NCETM). Their materials support teachers in planning small, connected steps that build secure understanding over time. This includes:
You can find more information below:
Arithmetic fluency gives children the confidence to work efficiently with numbers, recall key facts quickly and apply methods accurately when solving problems. To support this, pupils take part in short, daily practice that helps them build strong number sense and secure the foundations they need for more complex maths.
The Essence of Mathematics Teaching for Mastery
How Daily Fluency Practice Works
Why not try one of their daily math challenges:
Third Space Learning Daily Maths Challenge
The Multiplication Tables Check (MTC) is a national assessment designed to ensure that children have secure, rapid recall of all multiplication facts up to 12×12. Strong times table knowledge underpins later maths, helping pupils tackle more complex calculations, fractions, division, and problem solving with confidence. Times Tables Rock Stars is used consistently across the school to support children’s recall of multiplication facts.

Be sure to get your child’s log in from their class teacher to ensure practice can take place at home.

PE at Rushey Green
We believe that Physical Education plays a vital role in every child’s development. Through our partnership with Moving Matters, we provide a high-quality, engaging PE curriculum that supports children to become confident, active and healthy individuals.
Our PE curriculum (see below) is carefully designed to follow the National Curriculum, which aims to help pupils develop competence in a broad range of physical activities, stay active for sustained periods, and lead healthy, active lives.
PE lessons are inclusive, enjoyable and structured to ensure that all children experience success, regardless of their starting point. Through Moving Matters, pupils take part in a wide range of activities including:
This variety ensures children experience a broad and balanced curriculum while developing a lifelong love of physical activity.
The curriculum is designed as a clear learning journey from Early Years through to Year 6:
Across all year groups, children revisit and build on key skills, ensuring steady progression and growing confidence over time.
PE is about more than physical skills, through our curriculum, children learn:
We aim to ensure every child leaves our school with the skills, knowledge and motivation to stay active for life.

PSHE
Subjects
PSHE at Rushey Green Primary School - The Jigsaw Approach
At our school, we use the Jigsaw programme to support children’s Personal, Social, Health and Economic (PSHE) education. This places every child at the heart of learning, helping them to develop the social, emotional and life skills they need to thrive both in school and beyond.
Jigsaw is a whole-school approach, meaning that learning about relationships, wellbeing and resilience is woven into all aspects of school life - not just taught in weekly lessons. Through engaging activities, assemblies and shared language, children build confidence, emotional awareness and positive relationships with others.
The programme is carefully structured and age-appropriate, supporting children to understand their feelings, manage challenges and develop healthy attitudes. It also meets all statutory requirements for Relationships and Health Education.
By nurturing children’s wellbeing alongside their academic learning, we aim to help every child feel safe, valued and ready to succeed.
Jigsaw PSHE Overview 185 KB

Spanish
Subjects
Spanish at Rushey Green

Phonics
Subjects
Phonics at Rushy Green - Little Wandle
At Rushey Green, we use the DfE recommended scheme ‘Little Wandle’ to introduce reading and phonics to our children. This initially focuses on sounds around us and then moves on to introducing letter sounds (phonemes) which are represented by letters (graphemes).
There are resources to help support your child with saying their sounds and writing their letters. There are also some useful videos so you can see how they are taught at school and feel confident about supporting their reading at home.
Resources for Parents
Make sure to refer to the programme overview from Reception to Year 1 so you can stay aligned with the progression of knowledge and skills children are learning in school.

RE
Subjects
RE at Rushey Green Primary School - The Jigsaw Approach
At our school, we use Jigsaw RE to provide a rich and engaging Religious Education curriculum that encourages curiosity, respect and understanding of different beliefs and worldviews.
Jigsaw RE is structured into age-appropriate groups from Early Years through to Key Stage 2. Children explore a small number of carefully chosen worldviews each year through enquiry-based learning, allowing them to develop a deeper understanding rather than covering too much content. Christianity is taught throughout the school, alongside other worldviews such as Islam, Judaism, Hinduism, Buddhism and Humanism.
In Early Years, children are introduced to important ideas such as belonging, special places and stories, helping them begin to understand the diverse world around them. As they progress, pupils build their knowledge through thoughtful questions, discussions and reflection.
The programme is flexible and tailored to meet national guidance and local requirements, while also reflecting the diverse society we live in. It supports children in developing respect, empathy and an appreciation of different beliefs and cultures.
Through Jigsaw RE, we aim to help children become open-minded, thoughtful individuals who value diversity and are prepared for life in modern Britain.

Governors
Governors
School governors have a responsibility for supporting their schools, while also holding them to account.
At Rushey Green, Governors are actively involved in all aspects of school life and contribute time and energy to ensure the school continually improves. Governors share the school’s aims and values, and are keen to enhance the environment, provide the right resources and to see that every child receives the best possible education.
The purpose of the Governing Body is to help the school to provide the best possible education for its pupils.
They work closely with the Headteacher and the Senior Leadership Team to set the school’s strategic aims and policies and actively work to monitor, support and improve the quality of teaching and learning for all pupils. The role of the Governing Body is one of strategic oversight; governors are not involved in the day-to-day running of the school. That is the responsibility of the Headteacher.
Our Governors represent our wider school community: elected parent and staff governors, one Local Authority nominee and co-opted members from the wider community. They have a mix of skills, experiences and backgrounds to help provide the best possible support to the School.
You can contact the Governors by emailing admin@rusheygreen.lewisham.sch.uk.
Responsibilities
A Governing Body’s responsibilities cover three key areas:
To Provide a Strategic View:
Focus on the future
Set appropriate objectives
To be a 'Critical Friend':
Offer support and constructive advice
Be a sounding board for ideas
Ask challenging questions when necessary
To Ensure Accountability of the School:
The full Governing Body meets formally twice a term. Sub-committees also meet once or twice a term to focus on particular areas in more detail.
The two main sub-committees are: Resources, Pay, Learning and Achievement, and Behaviour and Inclusion. Other committees, panels and project teams meet when needed.
It's also important for Governors to see the school in action, and they make regular visits to classrooms, to speak with teachers and to join in school events and celebrations.
Governors take very seriously the role they play and the contribution they can make. Governors are expected to sign up to a code of practice agreeing to act with honesty and integrity, to keep up to date with training and to respect confidentiality at all times.

Rushey Green School Association
Rushey Green School Association (R.G.S.A)
R.G.S.A. is Rushey Green's parent teacher association. All parents and carers are automatically members when their child starts school and we are hoping for more parents and carers to become involved.
The R.G.S.A. has a long tradition of active involvement with the school arranging activities that have included: The Winter and Summer Fairs, book swaps, cake sales, and various fund-raising events. The money raised is used to provide extras and special equipment for the children that would not be affordable from school finances and to support local charities.
The Association aims to engage with all families and our local community and embrace the cultural diversity to make our children’s learning experiences more fulfilling and exciting.
Mission Statement

pageCache.text:
Breakfast and After School Clubs
Superkids Club Ltd
Superkids Club provides Wraparound care: Breakfast Club and After School club, for children aged 3 -11 years old who attend Rushey Green Primary school.
Based in the school hall, children have free choice from a wide range of activities that support children’s development and independence, whilst having fun and promoting social skills. Each day, the hall and pitch area is set up with a wide variety of indoor and outdoor activities including team sports and physical games led by a qualified sports coach; educational games, construction, home corner, role play, reading corner, arts and crafts and themed topics.
Early Years children (Nursery and Reception class) have a dedicated space with age appropriate resources and qualified staff to support and encourage their development and learning.
Children are supervised at all times by qualified and experienced staff who are DBS checked and first aid trained. All Superkids staff participate in a Safeguarding Children training programme.
Superkids Opening Times
Breakfast Club: 7.30am - 8.45am. £6.25 per morning. Enjoy a freshly prepared healthy breakfast ranging from multigrain cereals, yogurts, fruits, bagels, crumpets, muffins and toast.
After School Club: 3.15pm - 6pm. £13 per afternoon (£15 for nursery and reception class children). A healthy snack is provided with fruit, vegetables and fresh water daily.
All dietary requirements are met.
Ad-hoc Sessions: For families who require flexibility, one-off sessions can be booked on a pay-as-you-go basis. Ad-hoc sessions are charged at £1 above the normal rate.
Holiday Club: 8:00am - 6pm. £30-£32 per day. Breakfast and afternoon snack provided. Please bring a packed lunch and water bottle.
For more information - please contact us on 07732 305454, email admin@superkidsclub.co.uk, or visit our website:

Curriculum Overview
Rushey Green Curriculum
Our curriculum is based on the National Curriculum and is carefully planned and sequenced to provide an inclusive, high-quality education for all pupils, enabling every child to achieve and thrive. All learning is underpinned by our core school values: resilience, unity, self-belief, honesty, empathy and a yearning to learn.
When using any schemes of learning, we personalise them, and teachers ensure that units are adapted to meet the needs of the children. We use these resources to support planning and resourcing:
Subject
Scheme of Learning/Approach
Science, History, Geography, Art, DT
Our curriculum gives children a structured learning experience that builds knowledge steadily, strengthens key skills and helps them to grow into confident, curious learners. Children revisit key ideas throughout the year, which enables them to remember more and connect learning across subjects. Our approach to teaching the curriculum is designed to build deep, secure understanding by introducing new concepts in carefully sequenced steps, revisiting key ideas over time, and giving children meaningful opportunities to apply what they know. A deliberate focus on language, supported by explicit vocabulary instruction and the use of sentence stems in maths, gives children the words they need to express their thinking clearly and overcome learning barriers. Our curriculum is designed to equip pupils with transferable skills that help them become confident, independent learners. Alongside strong academic progress, it nurtures creativity, curiosity, and a broad set of competencies that prepare children for future learning and life.
To find out more about our curriculum please email admin@rusheygreen.lewisham.sch.uk FAO Nerissa Fisher.
